reading: Each straight red segment gets an 8-coloured diamond around it: a background cell at perpendicular distance D from a segment cell is filled when D is at most that cell's distance to both segment ends.

new_rows.name: diamond
new_rows.datalog:
lo_y(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
hi_y(O, max(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
lo_x(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
hi_x(O, max(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
hseg(O) :- lo_y(O, A), hi_y(O, B), A = B, lo_x(O, L), hi_x(O, R), R > L.
vseg(O) :- lo_x(O, A), hi_x(O, B), A = B, lo_y(O, T), hi_y(O, U), U > T.
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
diamond(Y, X) :- hseg(O), obj(O, Y0, X), lo_x(O, L), hi_x(O, R), bgc(Y, X), D = Y - Y0, D > 0, E = X - L, F = R - X, D <= E, D <= F.
diamond(Y, X) :- hseg(O), obj(O, Y0, X), lo_x(O, L), hi_x(O, R), bgc(Y, X), D = Y0 - Y, D > 0, E = X - L, F = R - X, D <= E, D <= F.
diamond(Y, X) :- vseg(O), obj(O, Y, X0), lo_y(O, T), hi_y(O, U), bgc(Y, X), D = X - X0, D > 0, E = Y - T, F = U - Y, D <= E, D <= F.
diamond(Y, X) :- vseg(O), obj(O, Y, X0), lo_y(O, T), hi_y(O, U), bgc(Y, X), D = X0 - X, D > 0, E = Y - T, F = U - Y, D <= E, D <= F.

why: every background cell inside the diamond spanned by a segment (half-width = segment half-length) becomes 8; nothing else changes

reading: The 9 coloured cells lying on the two diagonals of the 5x5 input are packed into a 3x3 grid, keeping their relative order and dropping the background gaps.

slots.cells: the non-background cells on the X-shaped diagonals of the input
slots.layout: row/column order preserved, background gaps squeezed out

why: out[i][j] is the i-th diagonal cell row-wise and j-th column-wise; corners from input corners, centre from input centre

reading: Whenever two cells of the same special colour (not 1 or 0) sit on one row or column, the cell exactly midway between them takes that colour.

slots.pairs: two equal-coloured non-background, non-separator cells on one row or column

why: every midpoint of a same-coloured pair on a row or column is painted that colour; nothing else changes

reading: The output tiles the input N times across and N times down, where N is the input's side length; every block is a full copy.
why: the output is an N x N grid of blocks (one per input cell) and every block equals the input

reading: A large shape cut off by the grid border is a 2x scaled copy of one of the small complete shapes; the output is that matching small shape cut out.

slots.probe: the large object touching the grid border (partly off-grid)
slots.test: candidate scaled by 2 agrees with the probe on all visible cells (up to colour)
slots.output: the box of the matching candidate

why: the output equals exactly one candidate's bounding box, and that candidate scaled x2 fits the visible part of the border object

reading: The input holds three 4x4 panels split by colour-2 columns; they are overlaid into one 4x4 with priority left panel (4) over middle (9) over right (1).

slots.panels: three 4x4 stripes cut by the full colour-2 separator columns
slots.order: left panel on top, then middle, then right
slots.output: each cell takes the first non-background value in that order, else 0

why: every output cell = first non-zero of (left, middle, right) panel at that position

reading: The top-left 4x4 quadrant is complete; each other quadrant is its mirror image (right: left-right flip, bottom: up-down flip, bottom-right: both), with its two colours remapped as shown by the hint cells in that quadrant (no hint means 0).

slots.copies: mirror images into the other three quadrants
slots.colour map: per quadrant, from the given hint cells: source colour at the mirrored position -> hint colour; unhinted colour -> 0

why: each quadrant equals the mirrored source with a per-quadrant colour substitution consistent with all hint cells

reading: All-background columns are removed and the shapes are shifted up or down so that each one joins end-to-end with the previous shape, forming one continuous chain from left to right.

slots.shift: each object moves vertically so its leftmost cell touches the previous object's rightmost cell on the same row

why: output width = input width minus empty columns; each object keeps its shape and is vertically shifted to connect to its predecessor

reading: Every coloured cell extends a line of its own colour straight down to the bottom border.
why: every cell below a coloured cell takes that colour, down to the bottom edge

reading: From the single 8 cell a staircase of 5s is drawn up-right and down-left (steps of one cell vertical, then three cells horizontal), clipped at the grid border.
why: the same staircase pattern, centred on the 8, appears in every output (clipped by the border)
